technical_validation.evidence: The task validator passed 12 of 12 checks. Ten stimuli and two critique charts rendered. A perfect-response self-check returned 100 percent accuracy and zero gap error for every display.

validation.scoring_self_check: pass: 100 percent higher-value accuracy and zero mean absolute gap error
validation.visual_preview: pass after dot, bar, table, pie, bubble, and critique inspection
validation.link_check: CMS, UW, PubMed, data-dictionary, and license links responded. The Cleveland and McGill DOI was verified in browser search; its publisher returned 403 to automated HEAD requests.

known_issues: Human visualization, clinical, accessibility, and independent-instructor reviews are pending.
The 10-trial exercise is too small and insufficiently controlled for generalizable graphical-perception claims.
Dot and bar stimuli use different axis ranges, which learners must name as a design confound.
Response timing can measure device, motor, language, visual, partner, and rendering differences in addition to display effort.
macOS and Linux clean-run verification remains pending.
